questions.q: What should slugify return when the input has no alphanumerics at all (e.g. '!!!' or '')?
What if `sep` is an empty string?
choices: Allowed: separators are simply removed, so 'a b' gives 'ab'

questions.q: What if `sep` is more than one character (e.g. '--' or '_x_')?
choices: Use it as given, one copy per run, and strip it from both ends as a whole
Only single-character sep is supported; raise ValueError otherwise
Use it as given, but ends are stripped one char at a time

questions.q: What if `sep` is itself alphanumeric (e.g. 'x' or '0')?
choices: Not special: collapse and strip by the same rules, even though it may merge with real letters
Leave as is and don't handle it

questions.q: Characters that fold away in accent stripping, like 'é' to 'e', stay as they are. What about characters that are dropped entirely, like '日本' or '€'? Should they count as separators?
choices: Dropped silently as now, so 'a€b' gives 'ab'
Treat them as non-alphanumerics, so 'a€b' gives 'a-b'
